questions.prompt: What is the momentum of a 1500 kg car moving at 20 m/s?
A 0.16 kg cricket ball has a momentum of 4.8 kg m/s. How fast is it moving?
What is the SI unit of momentum?
questions.explain: Momentum = mass × velocity, so kg × m/s.

questions.prompt: A 4 kg trolley at 3 m/s hits a stationary 2 kg trolley and they stick together. What is their velocity afterwards?
questions.explain: Momentum before = 4 × 3 = 12 kg m/s. After: 6 kg × v = 12, so v = 2 m/s.
questions.hint: Total momentum before = total momentum after.

questions.prompt: A 5 kg gun fires a 0.02 kg bullet at 400 m/s. What is the recoil speed of the gun?
questions.explain: Total momentum starts at 0. Bullet: 0.02 × 400 = 8 kg m/s forward, so the gun has 8 kg m/s backward: v = 8 ÷ 5 = 1.6 m/s.

questions.prompt: Why does an airbag reduce injury in a crash?
options: It increases the time taken to stop, so the force is smaller
It reduces your momentum before the crash
It makes you stop more quickly
It absorbs all of your momentum instantly
questions.explain: The same change of momentum over a longer time means a smaller force.

feedback.2: Stopping more quickly would need a bigger force.

questions.prompt: Two identical carts move towards each other at the same speed and stick together. What happens?
options: Momentum is lost, so they stop
They stop: the total momentum was zero
They move off to the right
They bounce back at the same speed
questions.explain: Equal and opposite momenta add to zero, so after sticking the velocity is zero. Momentum is not lost; it was zero all along.

questions.prompt: Explain why a cricket fielder moves their hands backwards when catching a fast ball.
questions.modelAnswer: The ball has a certain momentum that must be reduced to zero. Moving the hands back makes the catch last longer. Since force = change in momentum ÷ time, a longer time means a smaller force on the hands, so it stings less and the ball is less likely to bounce out.
rubric: The change in momentum is the same
Moving hands back increases the time
Longer time means a smaller force
questions.explain: Criterion D: applying physics to sport.
